arxiv-1911-01651.title: Weighted Min-Cut: Sequential, Cut-Query and Streaming Algorithms
arxiv-1911-01651.creator: Sagnik Mukhopadhyay, Danupon Nanongkai
arxiv-1911-01651.description: Abstract Consider the following 2-respecting min-cut problem. Given a weighted graph G G and its spanning tree T T , find the minimum cut among the cuts that contain at most two edges in T T . This problem is an important subroutine in Karger’s celebrated randomized near-linear-time min-cut algorithm [STOC’96].

arxiv-2101-01385.description: Abstract Stochastic control problems with delay are challenging due to the path-dependent feature of the system and thus its intrinsic high dimensions. In this paper, we propose and systematically study deep neural networks-based algorithms to solve stochastic control problems with delay features. arxiv-2106-12243.title: Bayesian evidence for a nonlinear damping model for coronal loop oscillations Facilities: SDO/AIA ( Lemen et al. 2012 ) NumPy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 )
arxiv-2106-12243.creator: Iñigo Arregui
arxiv-2106-12243.description: Abstract Recent observational and theoretical studies indicate that the damping of solar coronal loop oscillations depends on the oscillation amplitude. We consider two mechanisms, linear resonant absorption and a nonlinear damping model. We confront theoretical predictions from these models with observed data in the plane of observables defined by the damping ratio and the oscillation amplitude.

arxiv-2301-11463.title: Nik Defense: An Artificial Intelligence Based Defense Mechanism against Selfish Mining in Bitcoin
arxiv-2301-11463.creator: Ali Nikhalat-Jahromi, Ali Mohammad Saghiri, and Mohammad Reza Meybodi
arxiv-2301-11463.description: Abstract The Bitcoin cryptocurrency has received much attention recently. In the network of Bitcoin, transactions are recorded in a ledger. In this network, the process of recording transactions depends on some nodes called miners that execute a protocol known as mining protocol. One of the significant aspects of mining protocol is incentive compatibility.

arxiv-2304-08950.title: A User Study for Evaluation of Formal Verification Results and their Explanation at Bosch
arxiv-2304-08950.creator: Arut Prakash Kaleeswaran, Arne Nordmann, Thomas Vogel, Lars Grunske
arxiv-2304-08950.description: Abstract Context: Ensuring safety for any sophisticated system is getting more complex due to the rising number of features and functionalities. This calls for formal methods to entrust confidence in such systems. Nevertheless, using formal methods in industry is demanding because of their lack of usability and the difficulty of understanding verification results.

arxiv-2306-05515.title: PeFLL: Personalized Federated Learning by Learning to Learn
arxiv-2306-05515.creator: Jonathan Scott, Hossein Zakerinia, Christoph H. Lampert
arxiv-2306-05515.description: Abstract We present PeFLL, a new personalized federated learning algorithm that improves over the state-of-the-art in three aspects: 1) it produces more accurate models, especially in the low-data regime, and not only for clients present during its training phase, but also for any that may emerge in the future; 2) it reduces the amount of on-client computation and client-server communication

arxiv-2506-10102.title: Learning to Collaborate Over Graphs: A Selective Federated Multi-Task Learning Approach The work is funded by the European Union through the project 6G-INTENSE (G.A no. 101139266).
arxiv-2506-10102.creator: Ahmed Elbakary, Chaouki Ben Issaid, Mehdi Bennis
arxiv-2506-10102.description: Abstract We present a novel federated multi-task learning method that leverages cross-client similarity to enable personalized learning for each client. To avoid transmitting the entire model to the parameter server, we propose a communication-efficient scheme that introduces a feature anchor, a compact vector representation that summarizes the features learned from the client’s local classes.

arxiv-2506-13590.title: Agent Capability Negotiation and Binding Protocol (ACNBP)
arxiv-2506-13590.creator: Ken Huang 1, Akram Sheriff 4, Vineeth Sai Narajala 2, Idan Habler 3
arxiv-2506-13590.description: Abstract As multi-agent systems evolve to encompass increasingly diverse and specialized agents, the challenge of enabling effective collaboration between heterogeneous agents has become paramount, with traditional agent communication protocols often assuming homogeneous environments or predefined interaction patterns that limit their applicability in dynamic, open-world scenarios.

arxiv-2510-09633.title: Hound: Relation-First Knowledge Graphs for Complex-System Reasoning in Security Audits
arxiv-2510-09633.creator: Bernhard Mueller
arxiv-2510-09633.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Bernhard Mueller. Hound introduces a relation-first graph engine that improves system-level reasoning across interrelated components in complex codebases. The agent designs flexible, analyst-defined views with compact annotations (e.g., monetary/value flows, authentication/authorization roles, call graphs, protocol invariants) and uses them to anchor exact retrieval: for any question, it loads precisely the code that matters (often across components) so it can zoom out to system structure and zoom in to the decisive lines.

britannica-1911-pavilion.description: Article 'Pavilion' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 20), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. from which the word is derived from the French. The term is chiefly used of a tent with a high pitched roof, a small detached building used as a summer-house, &c., and particularly for a building attached to a recreation ground for the use of players and members. In architecture the term pavilion is specifically applied to a portion of a building which projects from the sides or central part.

pmc-12373941.title: Identifying genes underlying parallel evolution of stromal resistance to placental and cancer invasion
pmc-12373941.creator: Yasir Suhail, Wenqiang Du, Junaid Afzal, Günter P Wagner, Kshitiz
pmc-12373941.description: Stromal regulation of cancer dissemination is well recognized, however causal genes remain unidentified. We previously demonstrated that epitheliochorial species have acquired stromal resistance to placental invasion, correlating with reduced rate of cancer malignancies, identifying stromal genes correlating with depth of placental invasion called ELI (Evolved Levels of Invasibility) genes. Similarly, decidualization of human endometrial fibroblasts confers resistance to placental invasion.

pmc-12589267.creator: Lledó Rodríguez-Azorín, Aurelio Gómez-Cadenas, María F López-Climent, Vicente Vives-Peris
pmc-12589267.description: Main conclusionMultifactorial stress combination negatively affects citrus performance, especially when these plants are under three or more stresses, affecting citrus growth at different levels including phenotypic, physiological, biochemical and molecular levels.AbstractIn nature, biotic and abiotic factors affect plant growth and development. “Multifactorial Stress Combination” (MFSC) refers to situations in which three or more stressors occur simultaneously or sequentially on plants.

pmc-12823567.title: Spatial patterning of the epigenome during vertebrate gastrulation
pmc-12823567.creator: Ana Paula Azambuja, Megan Rothstein, Tatiane Y Kanno, Marcos Simoes-Costa
pmc-12823567.description: A central question in developmental biology is how embryonic cells acquire and store positional information during pattern formation. In vertebrates, this process begins with the localized activation of signaling systems that mediate axial specification. How these spatial cues are recorded within the regulatory landscape of cells has remained unclear.

pmc-13295617.title: Social Media Platforms and Sustainable Tourism Choices: The Role of Online Review Credibility and Cognitive Processing
pmc-13295617.creator: Anar Eminov, Natavan Namazova, Zivar Zeynalova, Elkhan Richard Sadik-Zada
pmc-13295617.description: This study examines how social media–driven information environments shape pro-environmental travel decision-making within the broader context of sustainable tourism and digital information expansion. It aims to explain how informational, cognitive, and evaluative mechanisms jointly influence behavioral intention by integrating perceived trustworthiness of user-generated content, ecological awareness, attitude formation, and cognitive processing bias within a moderated mediation framework.

pmc-13351625.title: Sociodemographic and gender affirmation factors associated with gender euphoria: a cohort study
pmc-13351625.creator: Charlotte Blacklock, Michelle Tollit, Carmen Pace, Bradley Elphinstone, Sav Zwickl, Ada Cheung, Ken C Pang, Simone Buzwell
pmc-13351625.description: SummaryBackgroundGender euphoria encompasses positive feelings associated with gender expression, identity, and affirmation, and is important for wellbeing. However, little is known about how gender euphoria is experienced by different subgroups within trans communities. Such knowledge could contribute to a more holistic understanding of trans health and promote more accurate and inclusive care.

pmc-13680817.title: Computer‐Assisted Hip Arthroscopy for Portal Establishment and Suture Anchor Placement
pmc-13680817.creator: Lingxing Jiang, Ming Hao, Mingxin Wang, Xiaoqi Kang, Zhanghua Tong, Jixiang Dong, Long Wang, Chunbao Li
pmc-13680817.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Hip arthroscopy is the gold standard for treating femoroacetabular impingement syndrome and acetabular labral tears. Portal establishment and suture anchor placement are crucial steps for ensuring the success of the surgery. However, because of the complex anatomy, deep location, and narrow joint space of the hip joint, the learning curve for establishing the hip arthroscopy approach and placing suture anchors for labral repair is arduous, with a high risk of iatrogenic cartilage and labral damage.

pmc-13700199.title: Effectiveness of the “Level-Points” online training model and influencing factors in enhancing scoring accuracy among surgical examiners
pmc-13700199.creator: Lina Zhang, Mengling Yan, Yiwen Qiu, Haolei Cai, Yunxian Yu
pmc-13700199.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEnsuring a standardized level of scoring capability among surgical examiners is crucial for the fairness and validity of competency-based assessments in standardized residency training. However, traditional in-person training models face significant challenges in scalability and accessibility. The aim of this study was to evaluate the “Level-Points” online training model for enhancing scoring accuracy among surgical examiners and identify its key influencing factors.MethodsThis study included data from the 2024 national surgical examiner training program.
